label: TACACS+
notes: TACACS+ Device Administration AAA (RFC 8907) over TCP port 49. The 12-byte fixed header of RFC 8907 section 4.1 is modelled; the body that follows (the START/REPLY/CONTINUE and REQUEST/REPLY structures of sections 5-7) is variable-length and, unless the unencrypted flag is set, obfuscated with an MD5 pseudo-pad keyed by session_id, version and seq_no (section 4.5), so it is not modelled. A TCP connection carries one session by default; once single-connection mode is negotiated in the first two packets (section 4.3), sessions are multiplexed on it and told apart by session_id. The anchor base 20 assumes a TCP header without options, the same fixed-header convention as the IP anchor.

fields.label: Version
fields.description: Version byte packing the 4-bit major version in the high nibble and the 4-bit minor version in the low nibble; the major version is 0xc, so only 0xc0 and 0xc1 appear on the wire. Minor version 1 is used solely by PAP, CHAP and MS-CHAP login; ASCII authentication, authorization and accounting all run minor version 0 (section 5.4.1).

fields.label: Packet Type
fields.description: Which of the three TACACS+ exchanges the packet belongs to; it fixes the layout of the body that follows the header.

fields.label: Sequence Number
fields.description: Per-session counter: the first packet of a session carries 1 and each subsequent packet increments it by one; odd values are client requests and even values server replies. A RESTART status makes the client begin again with a new session_id and seq_no 1 (section 5.4.3).

fields.label: Flags
fields.description: Unencrypted marks the body as cleartext instead of MD5-obfuscated; it is deprecated and must not be used in production (section 4.5). Single connection is set in the first two packets of a TCP connection to negotiate multiplexing several sessions over it (section 4.3). The remaining bits are unused.

fields.label: Session ID
fields.description: Identifier randomly chosen by the client for each session; it ties together the packets of one authentication, authorization or accounting exchange and seeds the body obfuscation pad (section 4.5).

fields.label: Body Length
fields.description: Size of the packet body in octets, excluding the 12-byte header; the bare-header error reply of section 3.6 carries 0.
